metadata.synopsis: Uma capitã aprende que ajudar a equipe pode significar falar menos e abrir espaço para a voz de uma nova jogadora.

scenes.title: The Loudest Voice
scenes.narration: Mika was captain of a small indoor football team. Before the evening match, she called instructions across the court. June, a new player, looked at her and then at the ball. "I can hear you, but there are too many words." Mika stopped. She wanted to help her team, but speaking louder was not making her message easier to understand.

scenes.title: One Idea at a Time
scenes.narration: The coach called a short break before the match began. Mika sat beside June on the bench and asked what would help. "One idea at a time. Tell me where you need me." Mika drew a simple arrow on a small whiteboard. June pointed to the open space beside the net and nodded. The picture was easier to follow than a long speech.

scenes.title: More than One Useful Voice
scenes.narration: Mika had two ways to share the simpler plan. She could stay on the court, use short calls and point to open spaces. She could also begin on the bench and let June explain the arrow to the team. "Being captain means helping everyone understand. It does not mean saying every word myself." June waited for Mika's choice.

scenes.title: A Pass They Both Understood
scenes.narration: Mika stayed on the court. Instead of a long speech, she used June's name and one clear instruction. June moved into the open space and received a pass. "That was it. We understood each other." The next move did not end in a goal, but their team kept the ball. Mika saw June ask for it again. They had found a way to work together.

scenes.title: The Plan in Her Own Words
scenes.narration: Mika began on the bench and handed June the whiteboard. June explained the arrow in her own words. She asked one teammate to show the movement, then checked that the others understood. "Captain, did I miss anything?" "No. You made the plan yours." When Mika joined the court later, she listened before speaking. Her team now had more than one useful voice.
